questions.question: In an isochoric process, $n = 1\ \mathrm{mol}$ of monatomic ideal gas absorbs $Q = 1247\ \mathrm{J}$ of heat. Find: (a) $\Delta U$, (b) $W$, (c) $\Delta T$.
questions.answer:
**(a)** At constant volume, $W = 0$, so by the First Law:

$\Delta U = Q = 1247\ \mathrm{J}$

**(b)** $W = 0$ (no volume change)

**(c)** $\Delta U = \dfrac{3}{2}nR\Delta T \Rightarrow \Delta T = \dfrac{2\Delta U}{3nR} = \dfrac{2 \times 1247}{3 \times 1 \times 8.31} = \dfrac{2494}{24.93} \approx 100\ \mathrm{K}$

questions.question: A rigid container holds $n = 2\ \mathrm{mol}$ of monatomic ideal gas at $T_1 = 200\ \mathrm{K}$ and $P_1 = 8.31\times10^4\ \mathrm{Pa}$. The gas is heated to $T_2 = 400\ \mathrm{K}$. Find: (a) $P_2$, (b) $\Delta U$, (c) $Q$.
questions.answer:
**(a)** At constant volume, $P \propto T$:

$P_2 = P_1 \cdot \dfrac{T_2}{T_1} = 8.31\times10^4 \times 2 = 16.62\times10^4\ \mathrm{Pa}$

**(b)** $\Delta U = \dfrac{3}{2}nR\Delta T = \dfrac{3}{2} \times 2 \times 8.31 \times 200 = 4986\ \mathrm{J}$

**(c)** Constant volume $\Rightarrow W = 0$, so $Q = \Delta U = 4986\ \mathrm{J}$

questions.question: What is the difference in heat required to raise $n = 1\ \mathrm{mol}$ of monatomic ideal gas by $\Delta T = 200\ \mathrm{K}$: (a) at constant volume vs. (b) at constant pressure?
questions.answer:
**(a)** Isochoric: $Q_V = nC_V\Delta T = 1 \times \dfrac{3}{2} \times 8.31 \times 200 = 2493\ \mathrm{J}$

**(b)** Isobaric: $Q_P = nC_P\Delta T = 1 \times \dfrac{5}{2} \times 8.31 \times 200 = 4155\ \mathrm{J}$

Difference: $Q_P - Q_V = nR\Delta T = 1 \times 8.31 \times 200 = 1662\ \mathrm{J}$

The extra heat in the isobaric case equals the work done by the expanding gas.

questions.question: A gas in a rigid container has its pressure doubled by heating. If the initial pressure is $P_0 = 1.5\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$ and initial temperature is $T_0 = 300\ \mathrm{K}$, find: (a) the final temperature, (b) the ratio $\Delta U / U_0$ for a monatomic ideal gas.
questions.answer:
**(a)** $V = $ const, $P \propto T$:

$T_f = T_0 \times \dfrac{P_f}{P_0} = 300 \times 2 = 600\ \mathrm{K}$

**(b)** $U_0 = \dfrac{3}{2}nRT_0$, $U_f = \dfrac{3}{2}nRT_f$

$\dfrac{\Delta U}{U_0} = \dfrac{U_f - U_0}{U_0} = \dfrac{T_f - T_0}{T_0} = \dfrac{300}{300} = 1$

The internal energy doubles (same factor as pressure and temperature).

questions.question: In an isochoric process, $Q = -800\ \mathrm{J}$ of heat flows out of a monatomic ideal gas. The gas contains $n = 0.5\ \mathrm{mol}$. Find: (a) $\Delta U$, (b) $\Delta T$, (c) the change in pressure if $V = 5\ \mathrm{L}$.
questions.answer:
**(a)** $\Delta U = Q = -800\ \mathrm{J}$ (internal energy decreases)

**(b)** $\Delta T = \dfrac{2\Delta U}{3nR} = \dfrac{2(-800)}{3 \times 0.5 \times 8.31} = \dfrac{-1600}{12.465} \approx -128.4\ \mathrm{K}$

**(c)** $\Delta P = \dfrac{nR\Delta T}{V} = \dfrac{0.5 \times 8.31 \times (-128.4)}{5\times10^{-3}} = \dfrac{-533.3}{5\times10^{-3}} = -1.067\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$

questions.question: An isochoric process is represented on a $P$-$V$ diagram. What does the process look like, and how does the area under the curve relate to work done?
questions.answer:
On a $P$-$V$ diagram, an isochoric process is a **vertical line** at constant volume $V = $ const.

The work done by the gas equals the area under the $P$-$V$ curve (from $V_1$ to $V_2$).

For an isochoric process, $V_1 = V_2$, so the "width" of the area under the curve is **zero**:

$W = \int_{V_1}^{V_2} P\,dV = 0$

No area is enclosed, confirming that no work is done in an isochoric process — all heat input goes directly into changing the internal energy.

questions.question: A $2\ \mathrm{L}$ rigid container holds $n = 0.1\ \mathrm{mol}$ of monatomic ideal gas. A $100\ \mathrm{W}$ heater runs for $t = 30\ \mathrm{s}$. Assuming no heat loss, find: (a) the heat added, (b) the temperature rise.
questions.answer:
**(a)** $Q = P_{\text{heater}} \times t = 100 \times 30 = 3000\ \mathrm{J}$

**(b)** Rigid container $\Rightarrow$ isochoric, $\Delta U = Q$:

$\Delta T = \dfrac{2Q}{3nR} = \dfrac{2 \times 3000}{3 \times 0.1 \times 8.31} = \dfrac{6000}{2.493} \approx 2407\ \mathrm{K}$

(Large rise because $n$ is small; the pressure would also increase by the same factor.)

questions.question: In an isochoric process, a monatomic ideal gas goes from state 1 ($P_1 = 1\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$, $V = 10\ \mathrm{L}$) to state 2 ($P_2 = 3\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$, $V = 10\ \mathrm{L}$). Find: (a) $T_1$ and $T_2$ (if $n = 0.4\ \mathrm{mol}$), (b) $\Delta U$ and $Q$.

During an isochoric process, the pressure of a gas triples while the temperature changes from $T_1 = 100\ \mathrm{K}$. At the end, $Q = 6000\ \mathrm{J}$ was added. How many moles $n$ of monatomic ideal gas are in the container?
questions.answer:
Pressure triples at constant volume $\Rightarrow T$ triples:

$T_2 = 3 \times 100 = 300\ \mathrm{K}$, $\Delta T = 200\ \mathrm{K}$

Isochoric: $Q = \Delta U = \dfrac{3}{2}nR\Delta T$

$n = \dfrac{2Q}{3R\Delta T} = \dfrac{2 \times 6000}{3 \times 8.31 \times 200} = \dfrac{12000}{4986} \approx 2.41\ \mathrm{mol}$

questions.question: A monatomic ideal gas undergoes a two-step process: first an isochoric pressure increase from $P_1$ to $P_2 = 2P_1$ at $V = V_0$, then an isobaric expansion from $V_0$ to $V_3 = 2V_0$ at $P = P_2$. If $P_1 = 1\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$, $V_0 = 5\ \mathrm{L}$, $n = 0.2\ \mathrm{mol}$, find the total $Q$ and $W$ for the entire process.
questions.answer:
First, $T_1 = P_1 V_0 / (nR)$:

$T_1 = \dfrac{1\times10^5 \times 5\times10^{-3}}{0.2 \times 8.31} = \dfrac{500}{1.662} \approx 300.8\ \mathrm{K}$

**Step 1 (isochoric):** $P: P_1 \to 2P_1$, so $T: T_1 \to 2T_1 = 601.6\ \mathrm{K}$

$W_1 = 0$; $Q_1 = \Delta U_1 = \dfrac{3}{2}nR\Delta T = \dfrac{3}{2}(0.2)(8.31)(300.8) \approx 750\ \mathrm{J}$

**Step 2 (isobaric):** $V: V_0 \to 2V_0$, so $T: 2T_1 \to 4T_1$ (since $T \propto V$ at const $P$)

$\Delta T_2 = 2T_1 \approx 601.6\ \mathrm{K}$

$W_2 = nR\Delta T_2 = 0.2 \times 8.31 \times 601.6 \approx 1000\ \mathrm{J}$

$Q_2 = nC_P\Delta T_2 = \frac{5}{2}nR\Delta T_2 \approx 2500\ \mathrm{J}$

**Totals:** $W = W_1 + W_2 = 1000\ \mathrm{J}$; $Q = Q_1 + Q_2 = 3250\ \mathrm{J}$
